stemMd: Five measurements have mean 18. A sixth measurement of 30 is added. What is the new mean?
explanationMd: The original sum is 5 × 18 = 90. Adding 30 gives 120 across six measurements, so the new mean is 120/6 = 20. The old mean represents five observations and cannot be averaged equally with one new observation.

distractorRationale.e: This averages the old mean and the new value without weighting the five old observations.
distractorRationale.a: This underestimates the increase in the total.
distractorRationale.c: This does not divide the new total by six correctly.
distractorRationale.d: This treats the added observation as contributing too much weight.
